answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable stake: before an agent may trade, it locks funds or compute at a single vertex of trust — a registry that checks the stake is real and unique. Sybil copies then face a hard choice: each fake identity needs its own stake, so flooding the network gets expensive fast, while honest agents keep one cheap anchor. Reputation earned at that vertex follows the agent, so a burned identity cannot simply respawn in a fresh oasis of new accounts without paying again.
